carousel.title: My Wife Got Violent and the Police Got Involved. Then We Found MCM.
Stan & Daniel Marmorstein
before: Ann's dementia escalated into a crisis the family could not manage alone.
after: MCM took the case, kept Ann home, and showed up at every emergency since.

carousel.title: The crisis was more than the family could handle alone.
carousel.text: Ann's dementia turned into a behavioral emergency.

carousel.title: They needed a team that wouldn't leave at the hard part.
carousel.text: When Stan had to call 911 and Ann was unresponsive, MCM didn't clock out.

carousel.title: They wanted Ann home, not in a short-staffed facility.
carousel.text: "Absolutely she can stay at home for the rest of her life.

carousel.title: They got caregivers who stayed.
carousel.text: Over the years a small, steady team stayed with them, Rowena then Margaret, supported by son Dan on overnight care and a nurse practitioner visiting monthly.

carousel.title: A son who came home to help.
carousel.text: Daniel Marmorstein moved back from Los Angeles thirteen years ago to work at NIH, right as his mother began to decline.
If we need you, you're there. It doesn't matter when it is — weekend, late at night. You're always there. I don't know how to say how valuable that is.
carousel.by: Daniel Marmorstein · son · the Marmorstein family, client since 2019
